items.title: Activities
items.text: 1. Activity 01: Desktop Museum

items.title: One desktop, one story, one class memory
items.text:
Welcome to our Desktop Museum!

Every student has a different workspace. Some of us have elaborate mechanical keyboard setups, some prefer a clean and minimal desk, and others surround themselves with favourite gadgets, plants, figures, or little reminders of home.

This activity is about collecting those personal details and preserving a snapshot of our time as UNNC Computer Science PGT students.

There's one extra challenge: we'll build this collection together using GitHub!

Never used Git? No problem. Never opened a terminal? That's fine, too. You don't need to know how to code to participate.

By the end of this activity, you'll have contributed to a REAL collaborative project, learned a little about how developers work together, and helped create a memory of our class.

items.title: 1. The mission
items.text:
Each student contributes one personal folder containing:

  • A picture of their desktop setup.

  • A Markdown file containing a short description and a few comments. (I recommend you give a bilingual version)

Our class repository is:

  • GitHub repository: MSc-CS-2628

  • Class website: MSc CS 26-28 Homepage

  • Contribution directory: docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/

Your finished contribution will look like this:

A01-DesktopMuseum/
└── YourNameOrStudentID/
    ├── index.md
    └── desktop-yournameorstudentid.jpg (all in lowercase)

The folder name can be your real name (like MattLee or SanZhang, it's recommended) or your student ID (if you don't want to publish you real name on the Internet). Please consider your privacy before using your real name or student ID in a public repository.

The workflow is simple:

  1. Take a picture of your desktop.

  2. Create your personal folder and Markdown file.

  3. Upload your files to GitHub.

  4. Submit a Pull Request (PR).

  5. Wait for your contribution to be reviewed and merged.

  6. Find your contribution on our class website!

Your job is to contribute your own folder, not to modify the website itself.

items.title: 2. A few GitHub concepts, explained simply
items.text:
You don't need to memorise these definitions. They're here to make the following instructions easier to understand.

Term In plain English Repository (Repo) The online project containing our class website and its files. Fork Your own copy of the class repository on GitHub. Branch A separate workspace for preparing your changes. Commit A saved set of changes. Push Uploading your saved changes from your computer to GitHub. Pull Request (PR) A request asking the project owner to accept your changes. Merge Accepting your contribution into the main project. Markdown A simple text format for headings, paragraphs, lists, and pictures.

Think of the process like contributing to a shared scrapbook.

You make your own page, submit it for inclusion, and the organiser adds it to the main collection. Your original work stays separate until it is accepted.

items.title: 3. Step 1 — Take your desktop picture
items.text:
Your first task is the most enjoyable: show us your workspace!

You can photograph your physical desk or capture a screenshot of your digital desktop.

Ideas include:

  • Your monitor, laptop, keyboard, mouse, and accessories.
  • Your favourite wallpaper or desktop organisation.
  • Your mechanical keyboard, keycaps, or mousepad.
  • Plants, figures, collectibles, or other decorations.
  • A minimalist workspace or a multi-monitor setup.
  • A laptop-only setup that travels everywhere with you.
  • And anything which can show your personality.

items.title: Image guidelines
items.text:
1. Use good lighting if you're taking a photograph.

  2. Make sure your main setup is visible.

  3. **Save your picture as

    1. desktop-yournameorstudentid.jpg
    2. desktop-yournameorstudentid.png
    3. or desktop-yournameorstudentid.webp

  4. Keep the image reasonably small so the website loads quickly. Around 1–3 MB is a sensible target.

items.title: Please protect your privacy
items.text:
Before uploading your picture, check that it doesn't reveal:

  • Passwords, authentication codes, or account details.

  • Private messages, emails, or personal documents.

  • Confidential university materials or student records.

  • Information about other people who have not agreed to be included.

Our repository is PUBLIC, so your contribution may be visible to anyone on the internet.

Participation should be voluntary. If you prefer not to share your real name, use an appropriate pseudonym instead. A student ID is not anonymous information, so don't assume it is a privacy-safe alternative.

items.title: 4. Step 2 — Prepare your Markdown file
items.text:
Next, create a file named index.md in your personal folder.

Markdown is just a text file with a few simple formatting symbols. You don't need special software to write it.

You can use VS Code, a plain-text editor, or any other editor that lets you save a file with the .md extension.

Just copy this template:

---
title: "My Desktop Setup"
comments: "true"
created: 2026-10-27
---

![My desktop setup](desktop-mattlee.jpg)

## About My Setup

Describe your setup in a few sentences.

## My Favourite Things

- Keyboard:
- Mouse:
- Wallpaper:
- Favourite desk decoration:

## A Message to the Class

Write a short message, a funny story, or a memory
you would like your classmates to remember.

Replace the example prompts with your own content. Feel free to change the headings and remove any questions that don't apply to you.

You can write a little or a lot. A few genuine sentences are more than enough.

items.title: A few questions to inspire you
items.text:
• Why did you choose your current wallpaper?

  • What's your favourite item on your desk?

  • Is your setup designed for studying, gaming, creativity, or relaxation?

  • What's one thing you couldn't study without?

  • Does any item on your desk have a story behind it?

  • What's one thing you would like to remember about your time at UNNC?

Your contribution doesn't need to be technical. A personal story can be just as interesting as a detailed hardware list.

items.title: How does Markdown display a picture?
items.text:
This line is important:

![My desktop setup](desktop-yournameorstudentid.jpg)

It tells the website to display the image file called desktop-yournameorstudentid.jpg.

Because the Markdown file and image are in the same folder, you only need to write the filename.

If your picture is named desktop-mattlee.png, use:

![My desktop setup](desktop-mattlee.png)

The filename must match exactly, including the extension and capitalisation.

items.title: 5. Step 3 — Check your folder
items.text:
Before uploading, make sure your files are organised like this:

YourNameOrStudentID/
├── index.md
└── desktop-yournameorstudentid.jpg

For example, if you choose the folder name MattLee:

A01-DesktopMuseum/
└── MattLee/
    ├── index.md
    └── desktop-mattlee.jpg

Your final folder name should be the identifier you choose, following the naming rules.

items.title: Final checklist
items.text:
• My folder has an appropriate name.
  • My Markdown file is named index.md.
  • My picture is inside the same folder.
  • The image filename in Markdown matches the actual file.
  • My comments are complete.
  • I have checked the image for private information.
  • I have not modified another student's contribution.

If everything looks good, it's time to submit your work!

items.title: 6. Step 4 — Submit your contribution using GitHub
items.text: There are two recommended methods. Method A is the easiest for beginners, because you can do everything in your browser without installing Git or using the terminal.

items.title: Method A — GitHub website (RECOMMENDED for beginners)
items.text: You will use your browser to create a fork, upload your files, and open a Pull Request.

items.title: A1. Sign in to GitHub
items.text:
Open the MSc-CS-2628 repository.

Sign in to your GitHub account. If you don't have one, create an account at github.com.

I suggest you create a brand-new account with your UNNC email address if you are a newbie.

items.title: A2. Fork the repository
items.text:
On the original repository page, click Fork near the top.

A fork is your personal copy of the class project. It lets you prepare changes without directly modifying the original repository.

Follow GitHub's prompts to create your fork.

You will now have a repository under your own GitHub username, with a name such as MSc-CS-2628.

items.title: A3. Create a branch
items.text:
In your fork, open the branch selector, which normally shows main.

Create a new branch for your contribution. For example:

add-mattlee-desktop

Replace mattlee with your chosen identifier.

A branch is simply a separate place to prepare your work. You don't need to understand the underlying technical details to use it.

items.title: A4. Open the activity directory
items.text:
In your fork, navigate to:

docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/

items.title: A5. Create your Markdown file
items.text:
Inside A01-DesktopMuseum/, use Add file → Create new file.

In the filename field, enter your folder name and filename together. For example:

MattLee/index.md

GitHub will create the nested folder automatically when you commit the file.

Paste your completed Markdown content into the editor.

Then click the green "Commit changes..." button, enter a commit message like this:

add mattlee desktop contribution

Choose the option to commit directly to your new branch, then commit the file.

Your folder now exists in your fork.

items.title: A6. Upload your picture
items.text:
Return to the directory you just created:

docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/MattLee/

Choose Add file → Upload files.

Upload your image, for example:

desktop-mattlee.jpg

Commit the upload to the same branch you used in the previous step.

Your folder should now contain:

MattLee/
├── index.md
└── desktop-mattlee.jpg

items.title: A7. Create a Pull Request
items.text:
Open your fork's main page. GitHub may display a Contribute button after you push or commit a branch.

Check these settings carefully:

  • Base repository: abotw/MSc-CS-2628

  • Base branch: main

  • Head repository: your fork

  • Compare branch: your contribution branch

Your changes should go into the original class repository's main branch, not into another student's fork.

Give your Pull Request a descriptive title, such as:

add mattlee to the desktop museum

You can use this description:

I have added my desktop picture and comments.

Contribution folder: docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/MattLee/

Click Create pull request.

Congratulations! Your contribution has been submitted.

The organiser can now review your changes and merge them into the class repository.

items.title: Method B — GitHub Desktop
items.text:
If you prefer a desktop application, GitHub Desktop provides a graphical interface for working with Git.

Download it here:

GitHub Desktop — Official Download

This method works on macOS and Windows.

items.title: B1. Install GitHub Desktop
items.text: Install the application and sign in with your GitHub account.

items.title: B2. Clone your fork
items.text:
Open your fork on GitHub and use the option to open or clone it with GitHub Desktop.

Alternatively, select File → Clone Repository in GitHub Desktop and choose your fork.

Cloning downloads a copy of the repository to your computer.

items.title: B3. Create a branch
items.text:
In GitHub Desktop, create a new branch, for example:

add-mattlee-desktop

Make sure you're working on this branch, rather than directly on main.

items.title: B4. Create your contribution folder
items.text:
Open the local repository folder on your computer.

Navigate to:

docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/

Create your personal folder and put the two files inside it:

MattLee/
├── index.md
└── desktop-mattlee.jpg

You can create and edit these files with your usual file manager and text editor.

items.title: B5. Commit your changes
items.text:
Return to GitHub Desktop.

Your new files should appear in the list of changes.

Enter a short summary, such as:

add mattlee desktop contribution

Click Commit to add-mattlee-desktop (the exact button text depends on your branch name).

This saves the changes locally.

items.title: B6. Push your branch
items.text:
Click Push origin to upload your branch to your fork on GitHub.

Pushing uploads your changes but does not merge them into the original class repository.

items.title: B7. Open a Pull Request
items.text:
Click Create Pull Request in GitHub Desktop, or open your fork on GitHub and create the PR there.

Check that the target repository is abotw/MSc-CS-2628 and the base branch is main.

Submit your PR and wait for the organiser to review it.

items.title: 7. Step 5 — Check your PR
items.text:
After submitting your PR, open it on GitHub and check the Files changed tab.

You should see your own two files:

docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/MattLee/index.md
docs/Activities/A01-DesktopMuseum/MattLee/desktop-mattlee.jpg

If you need to correct something, you can update the same branch. The existing Pull Request will include the new commit automatically.

You don't need to open another PR for each correction.

items.title: 8. Step 6 — See your contribution on the class website
items.text:
Once your PR is merged into the repository, your files become part of the original repository.

Zensical can then build the website, and GitHub Pages can publish the updated site.

The time required depends on the deployment workflow.

Visit the class website after the deployment has completed.

When your contribution is published, check that the image and comments display correctly.

You've now contributed to a real collaborative project!

items.title: My picture doesn't appear
items.text:
Check that the image file is in the same folder as index.md.

If your file is called desktop-mattlee.webp, this link is incorrect:

![My desktop setup](desktop-mattlee.jpg)

Change it to:

![My desktop setup](desktop-mattlee.webp)

Filenames are case-sensitive on many hosting systems, so Desktop-mattlee.jpg and desktop-mattlee.jpg may not be treated as the same file.

items.title: I can't upload files
items.text:
Check that you're signed in and that you're working in your fork.

If you are trying to upload directly to the original repository, you may not have write permission. Fork the repository and use a Pull Request instead.

items.title: I don't see the Pull Request button
items.text:
Open the Pull requests tab and choose New pull request.

Make sure your contribution branch has been committed and pushed to your fork. Then select the original repository as the base repository.

items.title: I made a mistake
items.text:
If your PR is still open, correct your files and commit the changes to the same branch.

If your PR has already been merged, you can submit another PR to correct your contribution.

items.title: My PR was merged, but the website hasn't changed
items.text:
The website may still be building or deploying. The organiser can inspect the repository's Actions tab to check the deployment status.

Also remember that a folder existing in GitHub doesn't necessarily mean it will be linked from the website's page.

items.title: I'm still stuck
items.text:
Ask the organiser or a classmate for help. You can also prepare your folder locally first and get assistance with the GitHub steps.

The goal is to learn together and create a shared memory, not to test your prior experience with Git.

items.title: 10. Our ground rules
items.text:
To keep the Desktop Museum welcoming and safe:

  1. One contribution per student. Please avoid duplicate folders.

  2. Respect other people's work. Only change your own contribution unless you have permission.

  3. Keep it appropriate. Your picture and comments should be suitable for a class website.

  4. Protect your privacy. Never upload passwords, private messages, confidential documents, or other sensitive information.

  5. Keep images lightweight. Help us maintain a fast-loading website.

  6. Follow the naming rules. Use an identifier approved for this activity.

  7. Participation is voluntary. Don't share information or pictures you aren't comfortable publishing.

  8. Ask for help when needed. Beginners are welcome.

Remember that removing a file later does not necessarily remove it from Git history, existing forks, or copies that others have downloaded. Think before you publish.

items.title: 11. What have you learned?
items.text:
Even though this activity doesn't require programming, you'll experience a real collaborative development workflow.

Your action What you've experienced Create a folder and Markdown file Organising a project Fork the repository Creating your own copy of a shared project Create a branch Isolating your work Commit your changes Saving a snapshot of your work Push your branch Uploading your changes Open a Pull Request Proposing a contribution Review and merge changes Collaborating on a shared project See the website update Publishing documentation

These skills are useful even if you don't intend to become a software developer. They can help you contribute to documentation, group projects, open-source projects, and other collaborative work.

Most importantly, the Desktop Museum will preserve a little snapshot of who we were during our time at UNNC: our workspaces, our personalities, and our memories.

Let's build our Desktop Museum — one folder, one picture, and one memory at a time.

items.title: About My Setup
items.text:
My desk setup is relatively simple. I have a few UNNC i-week merch charms hanging on the corkboard above my desk.

In the upper-right corner is a cheering light stick from Wonderful Us, this year's UNNC Class Song Competition. In the lower-right corner is a fan I picked up last Saturday (October 25) at a UN briefing event hosted by Soochow University. When unfolded, it displays the slogan “Together for Every Child.” I really like UNICEF and this slogan, partly because I still consider myself a child. I deserve to celebrate Children's Day, right? So, if you're reading this, please remember to get me a gift next Children's Day. 😉

I'm a big fan of Nintendo, so there's a Switch OLED in the lower-left corner that's been with me for several years. Unfortunately, I've been far too busy lately to play much. I'm not really into mobile games; I much prefer games like The Legend of Zelda, Stardew Valley, and Minecraft.

My Mac mini serves as my home server, running several self-hosted services, including Vaultwarden and Immich.

I also have a Xiaomi temperature and humidity monitor, and the monitor light bar is from Xiaomi as well. My 27-inch Dell monitor has been serving me faithfully for several years, too. Since it doesn't have built-in speakers, I had to add an external one.

On the right side is a CUKTECH charging station that I bought shortly after the semester started. It's been quite handy, and I especially like its retractable charging cables. The fan is also from CUKTECH. LOL, I guess I'm a bit of a CUKTECH fan!

At the far right is an IKEA tissue holder that doubles as a monitor stand. It's surprisingly practical and cheap, and I've already bought several of them.

After trying different keyboards, I still think the Apple Magic Keyboard is hard to beat. Touch ID and USB-C charging make it pretty much perfect for my needs.

My mouse is the Logitech MX Master 3S. It's fantastic, and I'd highly recommend it!

I wonder how much my desk setup will change by the time I graduate. Lately, though, I've come to appreciate the idea of long-termism more and more. For me, a good desk setup is all about simplicity and durability: keeping things simple, choosing things that last, and making the most of what I have.

items.title: 关于我的桌搭
items.text:
我的桌面比较简单，软木板上挂了一些开学时领到的周边挂件。软木板右上角是今年 UNNC 班歌大赛 Wonderful Us 的应援棒，右下角是一个上周六（10月25号）去苏州大学参加联合国宣讲会时领到的一把扇子周边，展开是“携手为儿童”的标语，我很喜欢儿基会，也很喜欢这句标语，因为我觉得自己仍然是个儿童，我需要过儿童节，是的。如果你看到，请记得明年儿童节送我礼物😉。

我是老任的粉丝，所有左下角有一台服役了几年的 Switch OLED，但是最近实在是太忙了，没有时间玩游戏。我是一个几乎不玩手游的人，比较喜欢塞尔达、星露谷物语、我的世界这些游戏。

Mac Mini 是我的服务器，我在上面部署了一些 Vaultwarden, Immich 之类的服务。

有一个小米的温湿度计，屏幕挂灯也是小米的，显示器是 Dell，27寸，也已经服役好几年了，由于没有内置音响，所以需要额外加装一个。右边有一个酷态科的充电站，开学之后刚买的，我觉得还是挺方便的，比较喜欢抽拉充电线的设计。风扇也是酷态科的，我是酷态科的粉丝哈哈。

最右边是一个宜家的纸巾支架，用来当显示器支架非常方便，物美价廉，我已经买过好几个了。

键盘用来用去还是觉得 Magic Keyboard 好用啊，指纹解锁 + Type-C 充电，基本没毛病。

鼠标是 Logitech 的 MX Master 3S，非常好用，推荐！

不知道毕业的时候，我的桌面会有什么变化，但是我现在越来越认可长期主义，简单、耐用就是我的桌搭理念。

items.title: 🎉 Weekend Forum #01: What's One Thing You'd Recommend to Everyone?
items.text:
Welcome to the very first CS PGT Weekend Forum!

As postgraduate students, we're all busy with lectures, coursework, and deadlines. But beyond our academic lives, everyone has something interesting to discover, enjoy, or share. Maybe it's a game you've been playing recently, a useful app that makes your life easier, a website you've bookmarked, a song you can't stop listening to, or even a restaurant you'd love our classmates to try.

So, here's our first topic:

Question

What's one thing you'd recommend to everyone?

It could be absolutely anything:

  • 🎮 A game you've been enjoying lately.

  • 💻 An app, software, or digital tool you find indispensable.

  • 🌐 A website or online resource worth bookmarking.

  • 🎵 A song, album, or podcast you love.

  • 🍜 A restaurant, snack, or food recommendation.

  • 📚 A book, movie, or TV series worth checking out.

  • ✨ Anything else you think more people should know about!
path: 🎉 Weekend Forum #01: What's One Thing You'd Recommend to Everyone?

items.title: How to participate?
items.text:
1. Leave a comment sharing your recommendation.

  2. Tell us briefly why you like it. A link or picture would be great, too!

  3. Feel free to explore other people's recommendations and join the conversation.

Warning

A small note on language: English is preferred so that everyone has an opportunity to practise English, but Chinese is absolutely welcome, too. Don't worry about perfect grammar or writing a long introduction. A few sentences are more than enough!

You never know — something you casually share might become someone else's new favourite thing.

Let's make this first Weekend Forum a good one!

Share something.

Discover something.

Get to know each other.
path: 🎉 Weekend Forum #01: What's One Thing You'd Recommend to Everyone?

items.title: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录
items.text: 关于作者：本文由宁诺计算机专业的一位硕士学姐匿名分享，记录了她参加 2026 年江苏省属事业单位统一公开招聘考试的经历，涵盖报名、资格审核、笔试、面试、体检及后续入职流程，希望为有志于参加事业单位招聘考试的同学们提供参考。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 一、个人背景与报考情况
items.text:
大家好！我是宁诺第 1 届 CS 专业 (24 Fall) 的硕士毕业生。

这次想和大家分享一下我参加 2026 年江苏省属事业单位统考的经历，希望能够给未来有意向参加事业编考试的学弟学妹们一些帮助。

我的备考经历比较特殊：此前曾三次参加计算机专业研究生考试，四门计算机专业课都经过了比较系统的学习。每年考研结束后，如果没有成功上岸，我也会尝试参加事业编考试。不过，虽然专业课基础相对扎实，我并没有完整、系统地准备过事业编考试。

最终，我选择报考江苏省事业单位计算机专技岗。以下是我的整个报考及备考经历。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 二、2026 江苏省属事业单位统考时间线
items.text: 首先整理一下 2026 年江苏省属事业单位统考的关键时间节点，供大家参考。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 1. 统一招聘流程
items.text:
事项 时间 招聘公告发布 2026 年 3 月 18 日 网上报名 3 月 21 日 9:00 – 3 月 25 日 16:00 资格初审 3 月 21 日 9:00 – 3 月 26 日 16:00 缴费确认 3 月 21 日 9:00 – 3 月 29 日 12:00 准考证打印 4 月 15 日 9:00 起 笔试 4 月 18 日 笔试成绩查询 5 月 9 日 资格复审 5 月 15 日 – 16 日 面试 6 月 6 日

特别提醒：以上是 2026 年江苏省属事业单位统考的时间安排。资格复审、面试以及后续体检等环节，各招聘岗位可能存在差异，务必以报考岗位的官方通知为准。

items.title: 2. 中外合作办学专业报考注意事项
items.text:
这是我认为宁诺同学尤其需要注意的一点！

对于中外合作办学项目以及留学人员的专业认定，不同招聘单位可能有不同的审核标准，不能简单地认为自己的专业名称与招聘公告中的专业名称相近，就一定符合报考条件。

我报考的江苏、上海等地招聘公告中，关于专业认定有类似这样的表述：

专业参考目录和招聘条件中都未列出的专业、留学人员的毕业专业，由招聘单位或其主管部门根据招聘公告中明确的专业条件、应聘人员所学专业课程、研究方向等认定是否符合招聘岗位的专业要求。

因此，建议大家在报名之前，主动联系招聘单位进行确认，并提前准备好以下材料：

  • 个人成绩单；

  • 学校出具的专业说明或专业证明；

  • 其他能够说明自身专业课程设置、研究方向的材料。

可以直接向招聘单位询问：上述材料是否能够证明自己的专业符合岗位要求。

我自己就遇到过类似情况：曾经报名义乌一所高校的岗位，但对方在电话审核后认为，我的专业是 Computer Science，而岗位要求的是 Computer Science and Technology，因此不符合报考条件。即使我提供了学校出具的专业证明，对方仍然没有认可。

所以，不要等到报名结束后才发现专业不符合要求，提前沟通非常重要！
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 3. 资格复审：一定要高度重视
items.text:
资格复审是整个流程中非常关键的一个环节，这里分享几个容易被忽视的细节。

第一，不要只等电话或短信通知。

有些招聘单位会提前通过电话或短信通知考生参加资格复审，但并不是所有单位都会这样做。大家一定要主动关注报考岗位的官方网站，及时查看相关公告。

第二，注意招聘通知可能发布在上级主管部门的网站。

我当时报考的岗位，其资格复审通知并没有发布在具体任职单位的官网，而是发布在了上级机构的官方网站上。

当时我连续蹲了好几天都没有看到通知，差点错过资格复审。等到真正发现公告时，只剩下周五下午的时间准备材料，确实有些紧张。

好在宁诺老师的办事效率很高，在老师的帮助下，我很快就准备好了所需材料。

第三，建议提前参考往年的资格复审要求准备材料。

尤其是一些需要学校出具的文件，最好提前了解办理流程。例如，宁诺的就业推荐表需要提前在相关网站填写，并经过辅导员审批。如果一时忘记了，也不用太着急，可以及时联系辅导员寻求帮助。

我的建议是：提前准备、主动关注、多留意不同层级的官方网站，不要把所有希望都寄托在招聘单位的主动通知上。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 4. 面试之后：体检与后续入职流程
items.text:
面试结束后，后续流程同样需要大家留意。

以下是我所在岗位的后续时间安排：

事项 时间 面试 6 月 6 日（当天公布成绩） 体检 约 6 月 29 日 二次体检 7 月 7 日 毕业典礼、领取毕业证 7 月 18 日 留服认证完成 约 7 月 22 日

这里也分享一个体检方面的小细节：

体检前，单位会提前打电话询问是否处于生理期。如果恰好处于生理期，部分妇科检查和尿检可能需要安排二次体检。

我当时正好处于生理期，因此相关项目安排了二次体检。按照我的经历，生理期结束三天后可以进行补检，具体安排仍需以体检机构的要求为准。

另外，我所在的单位要求取得教育部留学服务中心（简称“留服”）的学历学位认证后，才能进行公示及后续入职流程。

我的时间安排是：

  1. 7 月 18 日毕业典礼领取毕业证；

  2. 领取毕业证后立即申请留服认证；

  3. 约 7 月 22 日拿到留服认证结果；

  4. 随后电话联系单位，按照要求提交留服认证等材料，继续完成公示及后续手续。

因此，对于宁诺的同学来说，建议提前了解留服认证的办理流程，并合理安排毕业、认证与单位要求的材料提交时间。

items.title: 1. 笔试：计算机专技岗的考试内容
items.text:
我报考的江苏省事业单位计算机专技岗，笔试内容分为：

  • 40%：行测

  • 60%：计算机专业知识

由于我之前有三次计算机专业研究生考试的备考经历，四门计算机专业课都比较系统地学习过，因此在专业知识方面有一定基础。

我的实际备考安排如下：

行测部分

2026 年 1 月寒假期间，我开始学习花生行测，主要集中在推理部分。

计算机专业知识部分

寒假结束、开学之后到笔试之前，我陆陆续续学习了粉笔的计算机专业知识课程。

当然，这只是我个人的备考经历。我的情况比较特殊，专业基础相对扎实，所以并没有完全按照一套完整的考编备考计划进行复习。

如果大家之前没有系统学习过计算机专业课程，或者对事业单位考试的题型不太熟悉，我还是建议大家多参考其他成功上岸的博主分享的备考计划，结合自己的基础制定更完整的学习安排。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 2. 面试：专业相关的结构化面试
items.text:
我所在岗位的面试形式也比较特殊，是与专业相关的结构化面试。

对于这类面试，我的建议是：

  • 搜集往年真题： 可以在网上寻找往年相同或相似岗位的面试题，了解常见的考查方向。

  • 利用 AI 工具练习： 豆包、Kimi、DeepSeek 等工具都非常适合用来模拟面试、生成参考题目、分析回答思路。

  • 多进行实际表达练习： 不要只停留在看题和背答案的阶段，尽量练习完整、流畅地表达自己的观点。

最后，我想分享一个自己在面试中的感受：

无论前期准备得怎么样，遇到没有见过的题目时，也不要慌张。大胆地表达自己的想法，把气势拿出来！

有时候，最终的结果真的会给你带来惊喜。
path: 宁诺计算机硕士考编经验分享：2026 江苏省属事业单位统考全流程记录

items.title: 四、写在最后
items.text:
考编的过程并不只是笔试和面试，还包括报名资格审核、材料准备、体检、学历学位认证等一系列环节。对于宁诺这样的中外合作办学背景的同学来说，专业认定和留服认证尤其值得提前关注。

希望我的这些经历能够帮助到正在考虑考编，或者已经开始准备的学弟学妹们。

最后，祝大家都能找到适合自己的方向，顺利上岸！

加油！ 🎉
